slot.brief: Velocity–time graph of a body made of straight-line segments; find total displacement as area under v-t graph and identify where speed is maximum.

stem: A body's velocity varies linearly between the points $(t,v)=(0,0),(2,6),(5,6),(7,-2)$, with $t$ in seconds and $v$ in m s$^{-1}$. What are its displacement from $0$ to $7$ s and its maximum speed?

verdicts.working: Displacement is the sum of trapezoid areas: 6 + 18 + 4 = 28 m. The largest magnitude of velocity is 6 m s⁻¹.

working:
Displacement $=\frac12(2)(6)+(3)(6)+\frac{6+(-2)}{2}(2)=6+18+4=28$ m.\\
Maximum speed $=\max|v|=6$ m s$^{-1}$.

Independent check: Displacement is the sum of trapezoid areas: 6 + 18 + 4 = 28 m. The largest magnitude of velocity is 6 m s⁻¹.
solution:
Displacement is the signed area under the velocity–time graph:
$$\Delta x=\frac12(2)(6)+(3)(6)+\frac{6+(-2)}{2}(2)=6+18+4=28\text{ m}.$$
The maximum speed is the greatest magnitude of velocity, $\max|v|=6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
